stories.title: Rubio says US not under systemic attack after tech outages
stories.summary: Marco Rubio told reporters there is “zero evidence” that the recent series of technology outages—including grounded flights, banking disruptions and problems with Apple and Microsoft services—are linked or part of a coordinated attack. He said the United States is not under a systemic attack and that each incident is unrelated. Cyber‑security experts also said no evidence ties the events together, noting many issues stem from updates to aging infrastructure.
stories.why: The comment is intended to reassure the public and guide policymakers by confirming the outages are not a coordinated cyber threat.

stories.summary: Anthropic is preparing for one of the biggest stock market debuts in history, with the maker of Claude AI expected to command a valuation of around $1.4 trillion or higher. According to The Wall Street Journal, the company was most recently valued at $965 billion in private markets, setting the stage for a potentially significant valuation increase through its IPO.

stories.title: RBI projected to raise policy rate by 75 bps by Q2 2027
stories.summary: Analysts expect the Reserve Bank of India to increase its policy interest rate by 75 basis points in the second quarter of 2027. They also forecast headline inflation staying above 6 percent into early 2027 before easing, while GDP growth is projected to moderate to about 7.2 percent that year. Strong domestic demand and an emerging investment cycle are cited as supporting economic activity.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.title: Assetz Ltd receives SEBI approval for Rs 1,200 crore IPO
stories.summary: Assetz Ltd has obtained approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India to proceed with an initial public offering, aiming to raise about Rs 1,200 crore. The company cites a large land bank and a robust project pipeline in Bengaluru, and notes backing from investors such as AGP Partners as it expands into additional markets.
stories.why: The clearance allows the firm to raise fresh capital, which could draw investor interest and impact the Indian real‑estate sector.

stories.title: New Toronto councillors include housing advocates aiming to address homelessness
stories.summary: Toronto’s newly elected council includes several tenant‑rights and homeless‑advocacy activists who say they will bring outreach experience to housing discussions. Some observers question whether advocate‑turned‑councillors can materially shift Toronto’s housing and homelessness policies, but the rookie members say they have the political will to apply their advocacy expertise to the city’s affordability crisis. Diana Chan McNally, elected for Parkdale‑High Park after 12 years working with people on the streets, said she will push for policies that address affordability, health‑care access and give homeless voices a platform, while also prioritising transit and waterfront issues.
stories.why: Council decisions shape Toronto’s housing affordability and homelessness response.

stories.title: Russian strikes hit two Kyiv bridges, disrupt heating and water supplies
stories.summary: Russian attacks struck two major bridges in Kyiv, prompting Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko to report damage to critical infrastructure and overnight interruptions to the city’s heating and water services. In a separate video, President Volodymyr Zelensky shared footage of a missile approaching the Crimean Bridge, calling the operation “unprecedented” and saying it had been planned for weeks.
stories.why: The damage hampers essential services for civilians and underscores the vulnerability of Ukraine’s infrastructure amid the conflict.

stories.title: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making. Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good.
stories.why: This matters because it could affect economic conditions, trade, technology, public systems or international decisions.
stories.previousTitle: Ukraine damages Crimean Bridge, section collapses into water
stories.previousSummary: Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge with long‑range weapons in a multi‑stage operation, causing a portion of the double‑arched structure to fall into the Kerch Strait. President Volodymyr Zelensky called the attack “unprecedented,” and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge will be rebuilt. The bridge carries road and rail traffic for Russian forces to Crimea.

stories.title: India and US near completion of trade deal talks, signing pending
stories.summary: Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said the legal texts for a bilateral trade agreement are almost finalized, indicating negotiations are close to completion. The signing depends on the United States establishing new tariff rules and resolving ongoing Section 301 investigations. Both governments want to conclude the deal quickly to deepen economic ties.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.

stories.title: Google says Gmail is operating normally amid outage rumors
stories.summary: On Tuesday, Google posted on X that it is not seeing evidence of a broad Gmail service disruption and reminded users they can check Gmail’s real‑time status dashboard. The post was intended to counter reports of a Gmail outage that began circulating on X after a Downdetector post. The clarification arrived while Apple and Microsoft had recently confirmed service interruptions.
stories.why: It reassures users and reflects heightened concern about the reliability of major tech services.
